title: Fix streaming output token metering parity + add regression tests
author: Nadia Rahman
description: Context: We found a consistent under-count of output tokens for streaming chat/completions compared to the non-streaming path, which makes blended $/1M output tokens look artificially high for streaming-heavy workloads and breaks parity in the unit economics aggregation. Root cause: the streaming emitter was incrementing output_tokens from partial deltas, but skipped accounting for (a) tool/function-call argument tokens in streamed tool calls, and (b) the final “finish_reason” frame when the last delta was empty. In addition, the truncation path (max_tokens / server-side truncation) could exit early without emitting the final accounting event. Changes in this PR: (1) Move streaming output token accounting to a single authoritative counter that is updated from the same tokenization boundary used for billing/metering (token_count_v2) rather than from per-chunk heuristics. (2) Ensure we emit exactly one metering event per request with finalized counts (output_tokens, input_tokens, total_tokens) regardless of early exits, cancellations, or truncation. (3) Add a streaming/non-streaming parity test suite that replays recorded streaming transcripts (including tool calls) and asserts output token equivalence within 0 drift (exact match). (4) Add metric parity validation in canary mode: for 1% of traffic, compute output tokens via both codepaths and emit a debug gauge of diff; alerting will be handled in ENG-8429 but this PR includes the metric emission and sampling gate. Safety/compatibility: No API surface changes. Metering event schema unchanged; only counts become correct. This will change historical time series in dashboards going forward (no backfill in this PR). Rollout: ship behind feature flag metering.streaming_output_token_fix; enable in staging immediately; ramp prod 0%->10%->50%->100% over 24h while monitoring token_diff and billing reconciliation deltas. Notes: This is intentionally scoped as a hotfix to restore parity; follow-ups for retro/backfill and documentation are tracked in the unit economics workstream.
commits: metering: unify streaming token accounting with token_count_v2
gateway: always emit finalized metering event on stream completion/truncation
runtime: include tool call argument tokens in streaming output token count
tests: add streaming vs non-streaming parity fixtures (tool calls, empty final delta, truncation)
metrics: emit sampled streaming_output_token_diff gauge for canary validation
testing: Integration: streaming/non-streaming parity suite (exact match across fixtures)
Manual: staging replay with tool-call heavy prompt; compared metering events in ClickHouse
Canary: enabled 1% dual-count diff metric in staging (diff=0 across 25k requests)
rollout_plan: 1) Merge to main. 2) Deploy to staging and enable metering.streaming_output_token_fix=100%. 3) Validate: streaming_output_token_diff p50/p95 == 0; no increase in metering_event_drop_count; no regression in gateway CPU. 4) Prod ramp: 10% for 2h, then 50% for 4h, then 100% if stable. 5) Notify Finance + Unit Economics channel that counts will shift upward for streaming traffic, impacting blended $/1M output tokens trendlines. 6) Open follow-up to backfill historical aggregates if Finance requests QTD comparability.
review_conversation: Logan Wright: Can you confirm we’re not double-counting tokens when a stream is cancelled mid-flight (client disconnect)? I want to ensure we emit exactly one event and it’s the finalized count, not partial increments.

Nadia Rahman (author): Yes — the handler now routes all terminal paths (normal completion, truncation, cancel) through finalizeAndEmitOnce(); we guard with an atomic emitted flag. Added test case `cancel_mid_stream_emits_once`.

Caleb Johnson: The parity suite is great, but I’d like one fixture that includes an empty final delta + finish_reason, since that was part of the bug. Also please add coverage for server-side truncation hitting max_tokens.
Nadia Rahman (author): Added fixtures `empty_final_delta.jsonl` and `max_tokens_truncation.jsonl` and asserted exact token counts vs non-streaming. CI green after rerun.

Allison Grant: For the sampled diff metric, please keep tag cardinality under control. Don’t tag request_id; model+route+streaming flag is fine. Also please default sampling to off in prod unless flag is enabled.
Nadia Rahman (author): Agreed — tags are {model, route, region, tier, streaming=true}. Sampling is gated behind the same feature flag and defaults to 0% unless enabled.
Chloe Martin: Any chance this changes billing totals? If yes we should coordinate comms. Also, how does this interact with tool calls in the gateway vs runtime?

Nadia Rahman (author): It will increase billed output tokens for streaming tool-call heavy usage to match non-streaming (i.e., it fixes an undercount). The tool-call argument tokens now come from the same tokenization boundary we use for the final response object; details in the internal doc added in this PR.
Logan Wright: Looks good. Please add a brief note in the internal doc about known limitations (e.g., tokenizer version changes can still shift counts) and how parity tests should be updated.
Nadia Rahman (author): Added a ‘Maintenance’ section: keep fixtures stable, bump expected counts only when tokenizer changes, and run parity suite as part of release validation.
release_notes: Fixed an undercount of output tokens for streaming responses (including tool calls and edge-case final frames). Added regression coverage to ensure streaming/non-streaming token metering parity and emitted a sampled diff metric for canary validation.
